chunks: And from him, from Abu al-Husayn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mujawir, who said: Abu Muhammad ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi narrated to us, who said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated from his brother Ja'far, from his men, who raised it, saying:

I was with Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), and the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), was mentioned. Ibn Marid said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is the reward for one who visits your grandfather, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him)?'
He said: 'O Ibn Marid! Whoever visits my grandfather, knowing his right, Allah records for him, with every step, an accepted Hajj and a flawless Umrah.'
And by Allah, O Ibn Marid, Allah does not feed the Fire a foot that became dusty in visiting the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), whether he was walking or riding.
O Ibn Marid, record this hadith with gold water.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.عَارِفاً بِحَقِّهِ: Knowing his right (due to his status)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting Imam Ali (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes that Ziyarah to Imam Ali (AS) must be accompanied by *Ma'rifah* (gnostic recognition of his spiritual station) to yield the reward of a Hajj and Umrah per step. The hyperbolic phrase 'write with water of gold' underscores the immense, almost priceless value of this act, while the promise that the Fire will not consume a foot that touched the ground in his service highlights the intercessory power of the Ahl al-Bayt in salvation.
